name: Kernel-Associative Fast-Binding with Calibrated Abstention (few-shot)

answers_attacks.C42_hebbian_is_known: Attack (C42 gate A/F): 'gradient-free Hebbian fast-weight/associative-memory adaptation is classic meta-learning machinery (fast-weight programmers lineage) ... known-mechanism-A bolted onto crowded-scaffold-B'. STRUCTURAL FIX: the contribution is not 'Hebbian write'. The binding is posed as CLOSED-FORM kernel-ridge regression from frozen content features to schema-coefficient corrections, which yields a POSTERIOR VARIANCE for free. That posterior is exactly what fast-weight programmers lack, and it drives a calibrated abstention gate -- a genuine mechanism, not a rebranded outer product.
answers_attacks.C42_fragile_vs_lora: Attack (C42 gate F): 'the headline claim depends on the fragile bet that a single associative write beats LoRA/fine-tuning baselines ... else the paper collapses to an ablation'. STRUCTURAL FIX: the headline is NOT 'beats LoRA on nominal few-shot SR'. It is 'closed-form binding + calibrated abstention gives comparable few-shot SR at ZERO gradient steps AND zero per-task weights AND fewer confident-wrong actions on OOD queries'. Even if LoRA edges nominal SR, the abstention axis and the no-per-task-weights axis are distinct wins LoRA does not have.
answers_attacks.C45_crowded_basis: Attack (C45 gate A): 'MoS-VLA already does low-rank basis + few-shot coefficient fitting'. STRUCTURAL FIX: the schema-basis half is conceded as prior art (cite MoS-VLA/MOTIF, claim no novelty there). Novelty is placed entirely on the kernel-posterior binding + abstention gate, which MoS-VLA (closed-form L1, single global basis, no uncertainty, no fallback) does not have.

mechanism: Offline: a small shared schema basis over action chunks (VQ or PCA over the multi-task set -- CITED as prior art, not claimed). Few-shot adapt (10-25 demos): fit a closed-form kernel-ridge memory mapping frozen CONTENT features -> per-timestep schema-coefficient corrections; no gradient descent, no backbone touch, no per-task trained weights (just stored keys/values + one matrix solve). Inference: query returns coefficients AND posterior variance; if variance exceeds a calibrated threshold (query far from all demos) ABSTAIN and emit the base policy's zero-shot chunk. Final action = base schema + gated coefficient correction.
vla_bottleneck: Few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos (explicitly uncharacterized in the project), plus the safety failure where few-shot adapters over-commit confidently on states outside the tiny demo set.
mechanistic_story: Biological fast-mapping binds a new instance's content to reusable motor schemas in one shot without re-learning structure; the missing ingredient in prior VLA few-shot work is knowing WHEN the one-shot binding is trustworthy. Kernel regression supplies a principled posterior: near the demos the binding is confident and specializes the policy; far from them it abstains to the zero-shot base, so scarce demos improve in-support behavior without corrupting out-of-support behavior.
dimensions_improved: Data efficiency -- few-shot SR at 10/25/50 demos via closed-form binding (distinct benchmark: few-shot protocol).
Parameter efficiency -- zero trained weights added per task (only stored KV + a matrix solve), vs LoRA's per-task weight set (distinct axis, orthogonal to SR).

Robustness via calibrated abstention -- posterior-variance gating reduces confident-wrong actions on out-of-support states, measured as failure-mode composition, not aggregate SR (distinct causal path: knowing-when-not-to-adapt, which no fine-tune baseline provides).
integration_path: Slot between frozen content features and the flow-matching/L1 expert's conditioning; the correction is additive over a schema basis so it attaches to both stochastic (flow) and deterministic (OFT L1) heads. Per-task adaptation is a matrix solve (seconds); nothing retrained per condition.
diagnostic: <1 GPU-day, pre-registered, two-pronged premise kill. (i) Shared-basis viability: fit the closed-form binding on k demos, measure held-out-demo chunk reconstruction vs a LoRA fine-tune on the same k; if closed-form is far worse (shared-basis assumption fails for LIBERO chunks), dead. (ii) Abstention calibration: on held-out states, does posterior variance correlate with actual chunk error (reliability curve)? If uncorrelated, the fallback gate is useless and the distinct 3rd axis collapses -> kill. Both offline, minutes-to-hours, no policy rollout needed to falsify.
nearest_prior_art: MoS-VLA (global basis + closed-form L1 coefficient, single demo, no uncertainty/fallback); MOTIF/STAR/Primitive-Subspaces (VQ motifs + fine-tune/LoRA); fast-weight programmers (associative write, no posterior, no abstention). Delta: per-task-family kernel-posterior binding with a calibrated abstention gate on a frozen VLA.
novelty_risk: MODERATE-HIGH. 'GP/kernel adapter head' can be read as known; the delta is the abstention gate as a first-class robustness axis + gradient-free + frozen-VLA few-shot positioning. Risk: if the shared-basis assumption is weak (diagnostic i fails), the whole thing degrades to a worse-than-LoRA ablation. The diagnostic is designed to catch that before compute.

audit.note: second-surgeon batch engineered against recorded fatal attacks (answers_attacks field). No dedicated novelty audit — judge Gate A skeptically from nearest_prior_art/novelty_risk; winner gets a dedicated novelty sweep before writing.

gate_result.reasons: A: with the schema basis conceded to MoS-VLA, the residual claim (kernel-ridge posterior + variance-gated abstention) is standard GP/selective-prediction machinery a reviewer will map to VINN-style nonparametric imitation plus ThriftyDAgger-style uncertainty gating; not affirmatively new. F: the repositioned headline concedes LoRA may win nominal few-shot SR, so the paper reads as an efficiency/application study of known components in a crowded few-shot-adaptation area.

name: Disentangle-Repair-Bind (integrated build: S1 decomposition feeding S3 binding)

answers_attacks.bag_of_tricks: Attack (recurring, C4 R3 flavor): a mechanism spanning >=3 axes reads as 'a subtle multi-part ablation / bag of tricks' rather than one contribution. STRUCTURAL FIX: this is deliberately ONE learned object -- the metadata-disentangled nuisance/content split -- reused at two stages of one pipeline (repair the nuisance factor at inference; bind on the clean content factor for few-shot). The unifying thesis (a frozen VLA's robustness AND its few-shot adaptability are both limited by nuisance-entangled conditioning) makes the three axes fall out of one representation, not three independent hacks.
answers_attacks.three_distinct_paths: Attack (recurring, C7 R3): 'robustness, SR, generalization -- one measurement counted three times'. STRUCTURAL FIX: the three axes are measured on three DIFFERENT benchmarks with three different causal mechanisms -- held-out-factor robustness (LIBERO-Plus, projection), few-shot SR (10-25 demo protocol, clean-content binding), and calibrated abstention (failure-mode composition, kernel posterior) -- so no single number is reused.
answers_attacks.perception_graveyard: Attack (batch-wide): downstream monitors die because their inputs are corrupted. STRUCTURAL FIX: the repair stage is strictly UPSTREAM (nuisance projection before the frozen expert), the only intervention point the debates left standing.

mechanism: Stage 1 (S1): metadata-disentangled nuisance/content projector; at inference, project the nuisance factor to its clean marginal (repair), leave content free. Stage 2 (S3): use the repaired CONTENT code as the key for closed-form kernel-associative few-shot binding with calibrated abstention. Both stages share the single disentanglement adapter; backbone and action expert frozen; per-task adaptation is a matrix solve.
vla_bottleneck: Joint: LIBERO-Plus appearance robustness (Stage 1) and 10-25-demo data efficiency with safe abstention (Stage 2), unified by nuisance-entangled conditioning as the shared root cause.
mechanistic_story: A frozen VLA conditions on features that entangle rendering nuisance with task content. That entanglement hurts twice: OOD appearance shifts move the whole conditioning off-manifold (robustness), and few-shot adapters waste scarce demos fighting nuisance variance (data efficiency). One disentanglement fixes both -- project nuisance to clean for robustness, bind on clean content for data efficiency -- and the kernel posterior over the binding adds calibrated abstention.
dimensions_improved: Few-shot SR at 10/25/50 demos -- Stage-2 clean-content binding.
Calibrated abstention / confident-wrong reduction -- Stage-2 kernel posterior (distinct failure-mode measurement).
integration_path: Single adapter at the vision/connector boundary shared by SmolVLA/pi0/OFT-class VLAs; trained once on clean sim-metadata features; inference-time projection + closed-form per-task solve. No action-expert retrain per condition.
diagnostic: <1 GPU-day: run S1's held-out-factor diagnostic and S3's shared-basis + abstention-calibration diagnostic on the SAME disentanglement adapter. Additional gate: verify Stage 2 on repaired-content beats Stage 2 on raw-content (if repair doesn't help binding, the 'shared root cause' thesis is false and the two stages should be separate papers).
nearest_prior_art: Union of S1 and S3 prior art; nothing found combining metadata-disentangled upstream repair with kernel-posterior few-shot binding on a frozen VLA. Delta: the shared-decomposition thesis unifying robustness and data efficiency.
novelty_risk: MODERATE. This is the recommended single deliverable: cleanest >=3-distinct-path story and lowest reviewer surface because both wins trace to one representation. Risk: it is a two-stage system, so ablations must clearly attribute gains to each stage (built into the diagnostic). If either stage's premise dies in diagnostics, fall back to shipping S1 and S3 as independent contributions.

audit.note: second-surgeon batch engineered against recorded fatal attacks (answers_attacks field). No dedicated novelty audit — judge Gate A skeptically from nearest_prior_art/novelty_risk; winner gets a dedicated novelty sweep before writing.

gate_result.reasons: A: everything beyond S1's core is conceded-known machinery (S3's kernel head), so the case rests on combination novelty ('nothing found combining') with no dedicated audit — not affirmatively strong on its own. F: two-stage system with double premise risk and stage-2 novelty conceded invites the review outcome 'drop stage 2, resubmit as the S1 paper'; the candidate's own fallback plan to split into two papers concedes it is not one contribution.

name: Reconsolidation-Style Associative Memory for Perceptual Robustness
source_domain: cognitive science — memory reconsolidation / attractor dynamics
mechanism: A small (~5-10M param) modern-Hopfield/dense-associative-memory layer between the raw per-camera embeddings and the frozen backbone input. Offline, store a compact prototype bank (hundreds-to-thousands of clustered embeddings) of clean training-distribution viewpoint/lighting states. At inference, a perturbed observation undergoes one or two Hopfield pattern-completion steps that pull it toward the nearest stored clean-manifold attractor before the frozen backbone sees it.
vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse under LIBERO-Plus (viewpoint and lighting are the named worst factors)
mechanistic_story: Reconsolidation theory holds a retrieved memory trace is briefly labile and actively repaired against the current (possibly corrupted) context before use — a correction step, not a static lookup. A frozen backbone has no equivalent: a perturbed view feeds straight through. An attractor-based correction layer actively pulls the perturbed embedding back toward the nearest clean-training attractor before the backbone ever sees it — repairing the input rather than hoping frozen features generalize.
nearest_vla_prior_art: Closest are memory-augmented VLA robustness papers — MAP-VLA (2511.09516), MemoryVLA (2508.19236), SOMA (2603.24060) — and 'When Robots Sleep' (2606.17493). All retrieve/replay stored experience for in-context adaptation or continual-skill stability; none use attractor/Hopfield pattern-completion on the perception embedding itself to correct a single corrupted observation. Distinct from killed #2 (freeze more of the network): this adds an active correction module in front of the frozen backbone.
integration_path: Dense-associative-memory layer between per-camera embeddings and the frozen connector; prototype bank built once via a forward pass over training rollouts, few learnable params (~5-10M, mostly read/write projection) trained with a reconstruction/contrastive objective on clean-vs-perturbed pairs (synthetic perturbations offline). A few hours on 1xA100.
pre_flag: Adjacent to crowded memory-module-for-long-horizon area; differentiator is attractor pattern-completion for single-observation correction, not experience replay.

evidence_papers: MAP-VLA: Memory-Augmented Prompting for VLA (2511.09516)
MemoryVLA: Perceptual-Cognitive Memory in VLA (2508.19236)
SOMA: Strategic Orchestration and Memory-Augmented System (2603.24060)
Dual-Memory Consolidation with Sleep-Wake Replay for VLA Specialization
Vision Hopfield Memory Networks for Image Recognition (2603.25157)
audit.nearest_prior_art: MAP-VLA, MemoryVLA, SOMA, and the sleep-wake-replay VLA paper all confirmed as real, and all operate on temporal/demonstration history for long-horizon task adaptation (soft-prompt libraries, cognition-memory-action loops, episodic-vs-semantic consolidation). None apply Hopfield/dense-associative-memory pattern-completion to pull a single corrupted current-frame perception embedding toward a clean-manifold attractor before the frozen backbone sees it. Vision Hopfield Memory Networks exist for general image recognition but not wired into a VLA robustness pipeline.
audit.notes: Genuinely distinct mechanism target (single-observation perceptual denoising via attractor dynamics) vs. the crowded memory-for-long-horizon cluster (which is about temporal context/experience replay, a different problem).

gate_result.reasons: E: fails the >=3-dimension test — claims only robustness+generalization, which on LIBERO-Plus are the same measurement wearing two hats; nominal SR is at best unchanged (prototype quantization risks degrading it), novel-object generalization is plausibly HURT by snap-to-training-prototype, and it adds params/latency/compute rather than improving them, so the affirmative case is 1-2 axes, not 3.

name: Reliability-Weighted Habit/Goal-Directed Blending
source_domain: cognitive science — habit formation vs goal-directed control
mechanism: Run two parallel branches off frozen backbone features: a cheap 'habit' branch (low-rank flow head conditioned only on proprioception + previous action chunk, producing long smooth reactive chunks) and the standard 'goal-directed' branch (full vision+language flow-matching expert). A small arbitration head maintains a running reliability estimate of each branch (prediction consistency/error) and blends their predicted velocity fields per step, shifting toward the habit branch when reliable (cheap, robust to visual perturbation) and toward the goal-directed branch when novelty/disagreement is high.
vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse (LIBERO-Plus viewpoint/init-state) and long-horizon stage-transition failures
mechanistic_story: Daw et al.'s arbitration model shows animals weight a cheap cached (habitual) controller vs an expensive deliberative one by estimated reliability, not a fixed schedule. Under LIBERO-Plus perturbations the vision-conditioned branch's reliability should measurably drop while a proprioception-only habit branch stays stable for well-practiced sub-motions (transport, reach) — arbitrating by measured reliability, not a hand-tuned mix, should recover success specifically on the perturbation axes that collapse hardest.
nearest_vla_prior_art: No VLA paper found combining reliability-based habit/goal-directed arbitration. Found only VLA uncertainty-for-failure-detection (2606.20754; token-level uncertainty, OpenReview NX0euXAv98) and the neuroscience arbitration literature, never joined.
integration_path: Low-rank habit head (~10-20M params) parallel to the flow-matching expert, plus a ~1-3M param arbitration/reliability head reading recent per-step prediction-error statistics, outputting a mixing weight applied at the velocity-field level (convex combination of two velocity predictions is well-defined in flow matching). Habit head trains on demo chunks with vision dropped; arbitration head via short supervised/bandit objective. Backbone frozen.
pre_flag: Distinct from crowded 'dual-system fast/slow VLA' (which arbitrates by compute/latency budget, not measured reliability) and from killed #3 RTC (which smooths chunk boundaries within one decoder).

audit.nearest_prior_art: Caluwaerts et al. 2012 implements reliability-tracked meta-control arbitration between a cheap habitual/taxon navigation strategy and an expensive goal-directed/planning strategy on a physical robot; arXiv:2004.08830 and 2004.14698 do the same model-based/model-free reliability arbitration in more recent robot motor-learning settings.
audit.notes: The named prior art matches the core cognitive mechanism (measure each branch's reliability, shift control accordingly between a cheap habitual and an expensive goal-directed system) on real/simulated robots, predating VLA - this is a repeatedly-reused classical robotics idea, not a fresh joining as the candidate claims. Surviving twist: continuous per-step blending of two predicted velocity fields inside a frozen-VLA flow-matching architecture (vs. discrete strategy/expert selection in the prior art), evaluated for LIBERO-Plus robustness - real but narrower than 'no VLA paper found' suggests, since the underlying arbitration mechanism itself is not new to robotics.

F: a CoRL/RA-L PC sees a classical cog-sci robotics mechanism re-applied inside the already-crowded dual-system fast/slow VLA space; the reliability-vs-compute-budget distinction is too thin to survive as the headline contribution.

name: RD-IB — Rate-Distortion / Multi-View Information Bottleneck Adapter
mechanism: Insert a small variational information-bottleneck layer between the frozen SmolVLM2 features and the flow-matching expert, trained with a multi-view IB objective (LIBERO's multiple camera streams, or clean/augmented view pairs, as 'views') that keeps only cross-view-shared information and discards view-specific nuisance via an explicit MI Lagrangian (rate-distortion sweep over beta).
source_papers: Alemi, Fischer, Dillon, Murphy — Deep Variational Information Bottleneck, ICLR 2017 (arXiv 1612.00410)
Federici et al. — Multi-View Information Bottleneck, ICLR 2020 (arXiv 2002.07017)
vla_bottleneck: robustness collapse — camera-viewpoint (worst LIBERO-Plus factor, ~56%), plus lighting/distractor
mechanistic_story: LIBERO-Plus analysis shows viewpoint/init-state shift, not missing task understanding, drives failure, and this project's own linear probe shows frozen features carry sufficient action-predictive information (R^2=0.75) — so the problem is nuisance (view-specific) information entangled with task-relevant information. A trainable IB adapter squeezes out nuisance channels via a formal rate-distortion tradeoff without altering the frozen backbone.
nearest_vla_prior_art: DRIBO applies multi-view IB to image-based RL, not VLA, not frozen-backbone imitation, never LIBERO-Plus. No VLA paper found using IB/MIB as a trainable adapter for viewpoint robustness. Distinct from killed #2 (freeze the whole encoder) and killed #7 (VICReg anti-collapse for unfrozen backbone): RD-IB keeps the backbone frozen and adds a compressive layer to discard conceded-present nuisance info.
integration_path: Small variational bottleneck (mu/sigma heads + reparameterized sample, dim ~64-128) into SmolVLA's connector. Train with existing action loss + beta*I(Z;X_view) using camera views or photometric augmentation as paired-view signal, sweeping beta. ~2-10M new params, fits SmolVLA's ~20h/1xA100 finetune budget.

evidence_papers: Peng et al., Variational Discriminator Bottleneck (VDB), arXiv:1810.00821, ICLR 2019

'Learning Representations in RL: An Information Bottleneck Approach', arXiv:1911.05695
audit.nearest_prior_art: VDB (arXiv:1810.00821) already applies an IB/mutual-information constraint inside imitation learning to get invariant, robust representations; IB-for-RL representation work also targets nuisance-invariance. No hit combines this with a frozen-VLM+flow-matching VLA, multi-camera LIBERO views, or a beta rate-distortion sweep for viewpoint robustness specifically.
audit.notes: Surviving twist: multi-view (cross-camera) IB formulation as a bolt-on adapter for a frozen VLA backbone targeting LIBERO-Plus viewpoint robustness, vs. VDB's single-view discriminator-bottleneck use in classic imitation learning. Distinct enough to survive but adjacent enough that VDB/IB-RL must be cited as prior art, not claimed as absent.

gate_result.reasons: A: DRIBO (ICML 2022) already uses multi-view IB for visual-control robustness and VDB (ICLR 2019) already puts an IB inside imitation learning; the surviving delta — same objective bolted onto a frozen VLA connector and evaluated on LIBERO-Plus — is backbone/benchmark transfer of a 2017/2020 technique, not an actually-new mechanism. F: 'we added a variational IB adapter and robustness improved' is the canonical incremental-application paper in a crowded invariant-representation literature; absent a surprising mechanism it does not survive a program committee, and TMLR-style well-executed-application is below the stated Q1/Q2 contribution bar.

name: Two-State Fast/Slow Motor-Adaptation Filter
mechanism: A ~10-parameter, gradient-free two-rate state-space filter (fast state: high error-sensitivity/low retention; slow state: low sensitivity/high retention, per Smith et al.) applied as an additive corrective bias to the frozen flow-matching expert's output chunk. After each of the first few rollouts in a new setting (new camera pose, object, lighting), the filter updates its two states from observed action-execution error via closed-form linear rules — no optimizer, no gradients.
source_papers: Smith, Ghazizadeh & Shadmehr, 'Interacting adaptive processes with different timescales underlie short-term motor learning', PLoS Biology 2006
vla_bottleneck: few-shot data efficiency at 10-25 demos, plus robustness to systematic viewpoint/init-state bias
mechanistic_story: Smith et al. show human adaptation to a systematic sensorimotor perturbation is explained by two superposed linear processes giving rapid initial correction plus stable long-term calibration. A consistent camera-viewpoint shift or new-object-pose offset in LIBERO-Plus is structurally the same systematic bias their model corrects in a handful of trials, directly targeting the 10-25 demo few-shot regime. Learns no dynamics — a closed-form bias filter, outside the world-model exclusion.
nearest_vla_prior_art: On-the-Fly VLA Adaptation via Test-Time RL (arXiv 2601.06748) and RobustVLA (arXiv 2511.01331) adapt VLAs online but via gradient-based RL/fine-tuning of weights — a different mechanism class from a closed-form, gradient-free two-rate bias filter that never touches a weight.
integration_path: Stateless-between-episodes, ~10-parameter post-hoc corrector wrapping the flow-matching output in the inference loop; update rules run in microseconds. Pre-registered success criterion: k-shot (k=1,3,5) success on held-out LIBERO-Plus viewpoint/init-state, filter on vs off, same seeds — essentially free (no training run).

evidence_papers: On-the-Fly VLA Adaptation via Test-Time Reinforcement Learning (2601.06748)

Rapid motor adaptation for robotic manipulator arms (CVPR 2024)
S2-VLA: State-Space Guided VLA Models (2606.27872)
audit.nearest_prior_art: TT-VLA (2601.06748) and RobustVLA (2511.01331) do test-time/online adaptation but via gradient-based RL post-training of weights. RMA-style rapid motor adaptation (CVPR 2024, following Kumar et al.) uses a learned neural environment-factor encoder, not a closed-form two-rate linear state filter. No VLA paper found using a gradient-free, ~10-parameter two-rate (Smith et al. 2006) filter as an additive bias on a frozen flow-matching head's output.
audit.notes: Core mechanism (closed-form fast/slow state filter, no optimizer, correcting output not weights) is a clean transplant from motor-adaptation literature; nothing in VLA space matches. Thin in scope (10 params) but structurally distinct from all adjacent test-time-adaptation work, which is uniformly gradient-based.

gate_result.reasons: C: the filter updates on an 'observed action-execution error' that is unobservable at deployment — proprioception captures low-level tracking error (near-zero, the arm faithfully executes the wrongly-targeted command), not the perceptual bias; with demo replays the error collapses to a policy-vs-demo mean offset, at which point the two-timescale structure adds nothing over an EMA and the mechanism-to-metric chain breaks at its first link. F: a ~10-parameter additive bias filter (audit's own words: 'thin in scope') reads to a program committee as an EMA bias corrector with neuroscience branding, not a standalone CoRL/RA-L contribution.

name: Funnel-Gated Re-Inference (adaptive chunk horizon via prescribed-performance control)
mechanism: Wrap execution in a funnel-control monitor: define a scalar/low-dim tracking error e(t) (predicted-vs-realized end-effector pose from the last chunk, from proprioception) and a time-varying funnel boundary phi(t) that starts wide and decays. While e(t) stays inside phi(t), keep executing the current open-loop chunk (skip backbone passes); when e(t) approaches the boundary, force early re-inference. No neural net — a model-free high-gain feedback law used only as a re-trigger.
source_papers: arXiv 2302.01754 (Berger et al., robust funnel MPC)
arXiv 2310.15544 (Berger et al., funnel control with internal models)
Bechlioulis & Rovithakis, IEEE TAC 2008 (prescribed performance control, foundational)
vla_bottleneck: latency/compute (backbone dominates) and long-horizon drift (fixed-schedule re-inference lets error accumulate silently)
mechanistic_story: The funnel gives a formal, monotonically-tightening bound on allowable tracking error instead of a fixed re-plan interval. On easy rollouts the funnel lets the policy run the backbone far less often (cutting compute/latency); when a perturbation pushes the trajectory off nominal, the funnel catches it early — before it compounds into a chunk-boundary failure — and forces a fresh VLM call.
nearest_vla_prior_art: Closest is killed #3 (continuation-conditioned/RTC AR decoding, 2512.05964, 2606.13355) — but RTC changes the decoder architecture/training; funnel-gating is a training-free, architecture-agnostic runtime monitor deciding WHEN to call the backbone, applicable to flow-matching/L1/AR heads unmodified.
integration_path: Near-zero-parameter wrapper in lerobot's rollout loop around select_action/chunk-execution: track a scalar error from proprioception, compare to a hand-set/tuned funnel schedule, short-circuit into an early backbone call when breached. Only 2-3 funnel hyperparameters to tune; inference-only, testable in under a day.
pre_flag: Replan-cadence cluster (C20/C31/C42/C43/C51/C52/C29): adjacent to killed #3 (RTC) and crowded adaptive-chunking (DVAC, HiPolicy, AAC).

audit.nearest_prior_art: VLA-Corrector (2607.01804, found live in search, not in the candidate's own prior-art list) already implements the identical high-level pattern: a monitor continuously compares predicted-vs-actual state, and on persistent deviation it interrupts the current open-loop chunk and triggers corrective replanning, otherwise preserving long-chunk efficiency during stable execution ('event-triggered adaptive action horizon'). AAC/HiPolicy independently gate chunk length on prediction entropy. RTC/A2C2 solve the adjacent but distinct problem of smoothing chunk boundaries.
audit.notes: Surviving twist is real but narrow: VLA-Corrector's trigger is a learned Latent-space Vision Monitor + gradient-guided replanning (touches a trained module); C20's trigger is a model-free, gradient-free control-theoretic funnel boundary over a low-dim proprioceptive signal with a formal prescribed-performance guarantee. Framing/goal is now demonstrably crowded (VLA-Corrector, AAC, HiPolicy all published), so the pitch must foreground 'provably-bounded, net-free monitor' as the distinguishing claim, not 'adaptive re-inference cadence' itself.

gate_result.reasons: A: audit is PARTIAL at 0.25 confidence — VLA-Corrector (2607.01804) already ships the identical event-triggered adaptive-action-horizon pattern (monitor predicted-vs-actual state, interrupt chunk, replan), and the surviving twist is a trigger swap (hand-set funnel schedule vs learned monitor), not a substantial mechanism. F: crowded replan-cadence cluster (own pre_flag; AAC, HiPolicy, VLA-Corrector all published, the last missed by the candidate's own search), and the headline 'prescribed-performance guarantee' is hollow — a monitor-only funnel enforces nothing since triggered re-inference gives no bound that error re-enters the funnel, so the one differentiating claim dies under a control-theory reviewer.

name: Self-Conditioned Action Flow
mechanism: During training, with some probability run the action-expert's step with a zeroed 'previous clean-action estimate' channel to get a cheap x0-hat (no gradient), then re-run conditioning additionally on that x0-hat. At inference, each flow step reuses the PREVIOUS step's implicit clean-action estimate (available for free from v=(x-x0)/(1-t)) as extra conditioning — no added NFEs.
source_papers: arXiv:2208.04202 (Chen, Zhang, Hinton, 'Analog Bits: ... Self-Conditioning', ICLR 2023)
vla_bottleneck: long-horizon collapse (SmolVLA 49-71% vs OFT-7B 94%+ on LIBERO-Long) via reduced per-chunk estimation noise, at zero added inference cost
mechanistic_story: Standard flow matching predicts velocity purely from the current noisy sample and t, forgetting how earlier steps refined the estimate. Chen et al. show self-conditioning gives a large sample-quality gain at FIXED NFE because the network builds on its own running guess; the effect is largest at high noise, which for an action chunk corresponds to disambiguating the sub-goal before committing to fine motor detail. A better-conditioned per-step estimate reduces per-chunk noise that compounds across a long episode.
nearest_vla_prior_art: Past-Token-Prediction (2505.09561) and Training-Time RTC condition on PAST CHUNK boundaries across the control loop — a different object from the WITHIN-CHUNK running denoising estimate. No VLA paper found reusing the within-trajectory x0-estimate as conditioning.
integration_path: Modify the action-expert forward pass to accept an extra x0_hat input (zero-init on first call), concatenated with the noisy chunk before cross-attention; train with the standard 50%-probability self-conditioning recipe. Adds a small input-projection (~few hundred K params); same NFE, same data, fits the ~4h/20k-step finetune budget.

audit.nearest_prior_art: None found in VLA/robot-policy space; Self-Guided Action Diffusion conditions on proprioceptive/action history + VLM cross-attention, a different mechanism (external state conditioning, not within-trajectory reuse of the model's own implicit x0-estimate).
audit.notes: Self-conditioning (Analog Bits, Chen/Zhang/Hinton) is an established general diffusion trick being transplanted, not invented here -- but no VLA/action-expert paper reusing the free within-step x0-hat as extra conditioning was found across 3 searches. Distinguish clearly from Past-Token-Prediction/RTC (cross-chunk boundary conditioning), which candidate itself correctly separates.

gate_result.reasons: A: NOVEL-by-absence only — self-conditioning (Analog Bits) is a famous, widely-reused diffusion trick (e.g. RFdiffusion, RIN); this is a zero-adaptation transplant with no VLA-specific design, so a reviewer says 'known trick untried here', not 'actually new'. F: 'we added a standard training trick to a flow-matching VLA' reads as an ablation-grade increment at a CoRL/RA-L PC unless gains are dramatic; the long-horizon link (per-chunk sampling noise drives the 23-46pt gap) is itself unproven, weakening the pitch.
